overview: Manyamkonda Lakshmi Venkateswara Swamy Temple is one of the most revered hill temples in Telangana, located near Manyamkonda village (also called Oblaipalle) in Koilkonda Mandal, Mahabubnagar district — about 5 km from Devarakadra town on NH 167 towards Raichur, and ~18 km from Mahabubnagar. Dedicated to a Swayambhu (self-manifested) stone idol ('Chekkani Shilpam') of Lord Lakshmi Venkateswara Swamy (Vishnu) in a natural cave ('Kattani gudi'), with consorts Sridevi and Bhudevi, it is popularly known as 'Pedala Tirupati' (Poor Man's Tirupati) or 'Palamoor Tirupati', because devotees believe worshipping here bestows blessings similar to those at Tirumala. The hill was earlier known as 'Munulakonda' (after Munula = Saint + Konda = Hill) and was the meditation place of saints like Narasimha Yogi, Kasirayalu, Ettepu Ramayogi, Veerappaiah and Yanumaddhasu; it was later renamed Manyamkonda. The temple — believed to be ~500 years old and the first temple in Telangana to have ropeway access — attracts thousands of pilgrims, especially during its annual Brahmotsavam (Jaathara, Jan/Feb), Vaikunta Ekadasi and other major festivals.
summary: Manyamkonda Lakshmi Venkateswara Swamy Temple is a Swayambhu hilltop Vaishnavite shrine in Koilkonda Mandal, Mahabubnagar district, Telangana (~5 km from Devarakadra on NH 167, ~18 km from Mahabubnagar), dedicated to Lord Lakshmi Venkateswara with consorts Sridevi and Bhudevi in a natural cave (Kattani gudi). Believed to be ~500 years old and the first temple in Telangana with ropeway access, it is popularly called 'Pedala Tirupati' / 'Palamoor Tirupati' / 'Telangana Tirupati' because devotees believe worship here grants blessings akin to Tirumala. The hill, originally named Munulakonda, was the meditation place of saints Narasimha Yogi, Kasirayalu, Ettepu Ramayogi, Veerappaiah and Yanumaddhasu. It draws thousands during its annual Jaathara (Brahmotsavam, Jan/Feb) and Vaikunta Ekadasi.

history.content: The temple's history dates back several centuries (believed to be ~500 years old). The hill was earlier known as 'Munulakonda' (from Munula = Saint + Konda = Hill in Telugu), because it was the meditation place of several saints and spiritual gurus, including Narasimha Yogi, Kasirayalu, Ettepu Ramayogi, Veerappaiah and Yanumaddhasu. Over time, the hill came to be called Manyamkonda. Per local belief, Lord Venkateswara manifested himself on Manyamkonda Hill to bless devotees who were unable to undertake the arduous Tirumala pilgrimage — the origin of the temple's popular name 'Pedala Tirupati' (Poor Man's Tirupati) / 'Palamoor Tirupati'. The presiding deity is a Swayambhu (self-manifested) stone idol ('Chekkani Shilpam') in a natural cave ('Kattani gudi'), with consorts Sridevi (Lakshmi) and Bhudevi. A separate Shiva temple exists in the caves near the main shrine, and an Alivelu Manga Temple (Padmavati-like) stands at the starting point of the Ghat road. The temple was the first in Telangana to have ropeway access, and it has been renovated periodically by devotees and the Telangana Endowments Department to preserve its spiritual and cultural heritage.

sthala_puranam: The hill was originally known as 'Munulakonda' — 'Munula' (saint) + 'Konda' (hill) in Telugu — because of the many saints who meditated there, including Narasimha Yogi, Kasirayalu, Ettepu Ramayogi, Veerappaiah and Yanumaddhasu. Per local tradition, Lord Venkateswara later manifested himself on the hilltop as a Swayambhu stone idol ('Chekkani Shilpam') in a natural cave ('Kattani gudi') to bless devotees who could not undertake the arduous pilgrimage to Tirumala. This gave the temple its popular name 'Pedala Tirupati' (Poor Man's Tirupati) / 'Palamoor Tirupati', signifying that the blessings of Tirumala's Venkateswara are accessible to all at Manyamkonda. The temple also has a separate Shiva temple in the caves nearby, and a Tavvani Koneru (naturally formed lake).
religious_significance: Manyamkonda is considered one of the most sacred Vaishnavite shrines in Telangana. It is known as 'Pedala Tirupati' (Poor Man's Tirupati) / 'Palamoor Tirupati' / 'Telangana Tirupati' because devotees believe worshipping here bestows blessings similar to those received at Tirumala, making it an accessible pilgrimage destination for all — particularly those for whom the Tirumala pilgrimage is difficult. The Swayambhu form of the deity, the natural cave setting, and the ropeway access reinforce its status as a 'miracle' hill shrine.
spiritual_significance: Devotees believe worshipping Lord Venkateswara here removes obstacles, fulfils wishes, and brings prosperity, health and spiritual well-being. Many visit before important events such as marriages, examinations and new business ventures. The ropeway access to the hilltop shrine is itself considered a unique blessing, and the cave temple (Kattani gudi) is believed to be a powerful site for meditation, in the tradition of the saints who preceded the temple.

miracles_and_devotee_experiences: The Swayambhu self-manifestation of Lord Venkateswara on Manyamkonda Hill in the natural Kattani gudi cave.
Devotees believe worship here grants blessings comparable to those at Tirumala, hence the name 'Pedala Tirupati' / 'Palamoor Tirupati'.
The hilltop's ropeway access is itself considered a unique blessing and engineering feat for a 500-year-old hill shrine.
architecture: The temple is built in traditional South Indian temple architecture atop a scenic hill. The entrance is marked by a beautifully decorated Rajagopuram with images of gods and goddesses carved on it. The presiding deity is a Swayambhu stone idol in the natural cave ('Kattani gudi'); there is also a Koneru (sacred pond) within the complex. The complex includes a spacious mandapam, shrines for Goddess Lakshmi, Lord Hanuman, Lord Garuda, Lord Ganesha and the Alwars / Vaishnavite saints. The complex also has a separate Lord Shiva temple in the caves, and an Alivelu Manga Temple at the base of the hill (at the starting point of the Ghat road). A ropeway provides access to the hilltop — the first in Telangana.

dress_code: Traditional and modest attire is recommended for all devotees. Visitors should avoid shorts, sleeveless clothing and torn or inappropriate attire. Devotees participating in special sevas are encouraged to wear traditional Indian clothing. Per general Telugu temple convention, men often wear dhoti (and may remove the shirt at the inner sanctum); women wear sarees or salwar suits. Footwear is removed at the entrance.

best_time_to_visit: Visit early in the morning for a peaceful darshan; weekdays are generally less crowded. Carry drinking water while climbing the hill steps or taking the ropeway. During Brahmotsavam (Jaathara, Jan/Feb) and Vaikunta Ekadasi, arrive early due to heavy pilgrim turnout — most vibrant but most crowded. October to March is the most pleasant weather window for the surrounding hill region.

travel.road: Located in Koilkonda Mandal, Mahabubnagar district, ~5 km from Devarakadra town on NH 167 towards Raichur, and ~18 km from Mahabubnagar. Well connected by TSRTC buses and private vehicles from Mahabubnagar, Hyderabad, Jadcherla and nearby towns. Buses run from Hyderabad, Mahabubnagar and Raichur up to Manyamkonda village, from where autos are available to reach the temple via the Ghat road. Two routes to the hilltop: Ghat road (for vehicles) and traditional stone steps (for those who prefer the trek).

introduction.en: Manyamkonda Lakshmi Venkateswara Swamy Temple is one of the most revered hill temples in Telangana, located near Manyamkonda village in Mahabubnagar district — about 18 kilometres from Mahabubnagar on NH 167 towards Raichur. Dedicated to a Swayambhu form of Lord Lakshmi Venkateswara in a natural cave on Manyamkonda Hill, it is popularly known as 'Pedala Tirupati', the Poor Man's Tirupati, because devotees believe worshipping here bestows blessings similar to those at Tirumala. The hill, originally called Munulakonda, was the meditation place of several saints and is the first temple in Telangana to have ropeway access.

history.en: The temple is believed to be around 500 years old. The hill was earlier known as Munulakonda — 'Munula' (saint) and 'Konda' (hill) in Telugu — because of the saints who meditated there, including Narasimha Yogi, Kasirayalu, Ettepu Ramayogi, Veerappaiah and Yanumaddhasu. Per local tradition, Lord Venkateswara later manifested himself on the hilltop as a Swayambhu stone idol in a natural cave to bless devotees unable to undertake the Tirumala pilgrimage — the origin of the temple's popular name Pedala Tirupati or Palamoor Tirupati. The temple was the first in Telangana to have ropeway access.

travel_guide.en: Manyamkonda Temple is in Koilkonda Mandal, Mahabubnagar district, about 5 kilometres from Devarakadra on NH 167, and about 18 kilometres from Mahabubnagar town. Buses run from Hyderabad, Mahabubnagar and Raichur up to Manyamkonda village, from where autos are available to reach the temple via the Ghat road. The nearest railway station is Mahabubnagar, and the nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad, about 110 kilometres away. The JustDial official listing shows 6:30 AM to 12:30 PM and 3:00 PM to 8:30 PM daily; the ropeway provides easy access to the hilltop. The most auspicious time to visit is the annual Jaathara in January or February.

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: Per the JustDial official listing: 6:30 AM–12:30 PM and 3:00 PM–8:30 PM daily (Mon–Sun). Other sources give slightly different windows (6:00 AM–1:00 PM and 3:00 PM–8:00 PM per user doc; 8:00 AM–12:30 PM and 2:00 PM–8:30 PM per Tripadvisor Mahbubnagar listing). The morning start time varies from 6:00 AM to 8:00 AM across sources; confirm locally. Hours are extended during the annual Jaathara (Brahmotsavam, Jan/Feb) and Vaikunta Ekadasi.

faq.question: Is there any entry fee?
faq.answer: No. General darshan is free for all devotees. Ropeway access may involve a small fee (not published in any source reviewed).

faq.question: Why is Manyamkonda Temple called Pedala Tirupati?
faq.answer: Because devotees believe worshipping Lord Venkateswara here offers blessings similar to those of Tirumala, making it an accessible pilgrimage destination — hence 'Pedala Tirupati' (Poor Man's Tirupati). It is also called 'Palamoor Tirupati' and 'Telangana Tirupati'.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped here?
faq.answer: The presiding deity is Lord Lakshmi Venkateswara Swamy, a Swayambhu (self-manifested) stone idol ('Chekkani Shilpam') in a natural cave ('Kattani gudi') on Manyamkonda Hill, with consorts Goddess Sridevi (Lakshmi) and Goddess Bhudevi. There are also shrines to Lord Hanuman, Lord Garuda, Lord Ganesha, the Alwars / Vaishnavite saints, and a separate Lord Shiva temple in the caves.

faq.question: What is unique about this temple?
faq.answer: Three things make it unique: (1) It is the first temple in Telangana to have ropeway access; (2) the presiding deity is a Swayambhu stone idol in a natural cave (Kattani gudi) on a hill, with a Tavvani Koneru (naturally formed lake); (3) it sits on Munulakonda / Manyamkonda Hill, the meditation place of saints Narasimha Yogi, Kasirayalu, Ettepu Ramayogi, Veerappaiah and Yanumaddhasu.

faq.question: Which festivals are celebrated?
faq.answer: Major festivals include the Annual Brahmotsavam (Jaathara, Jan/Feb), Vaikunta Ekadasi, Mukkoti Ekadasi, Sri Rama Navami, Krishna Janmashtami, Ugadi, and Deepavali.

faq.question: Is parking available?
faq.answer: Yes. Parking facilities are available near the temple premises / Ghat road starting point for devotees.

faq.question: How can I reach the temple?
faq.answer: By road from Mahabubnagar (~18 km on NH 167) or Hyderabad (~110 km). Buses run from Hyderabad, Mahabubnagar and Raichur to Manyamkonda village; autos are available from the village to the Ghat road. Two routes to the hilltop: Ghat road (for vehicles) and traditional stone steps (trekking). A ropeway provides easy access — the first ropeway-accessed temple in Telangana. The nearest railway station is Mahabubnagar, and the nearest airport is Hyderabad (~110 km).

faq.question: Is accommodation available nearby?
faq.answer: Yes. Accommodation is available in Mahabubnagar town (~18 km), at temple guest houses (subject to availability), and at private lodges and hotels in nearby areas like Devarakadra (~5 km). Advance booking is recommended during Brahmotsavam and Vaikunta Ekadasi.

faq.question: What are the nearby attractions?
faq.answer: Popular nearby attractions include Koilkonda Fort, Pillalamarri Banyan Tree, Jurala Project, Alampur Jogulamba Temple (Shakti Peetha), Mallela Theertham Waterfall, Mahabubnagar Town, Koilsagar Project, and Devarakadra town.

faq.question: What facilities are available at the temple?
faq.answer: The temple provides parking, drinking water, restrooms, a shoe stand, seating areas, a prasadam counter, an information centre, first aid, security personnel, and limited wheelchair access in selected areas. Ropeway access to the hilltop is the temple's signature facility.
